repository_card.frontier: The filled-SSH identity is exact in its stated model; the maintenance exponent carries the Davies envelope and invariance condition.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: Compare conserved slow-mode reconstructions and gauge-bath Zeno effects with filled-sector leakage. Dictionary: population/filling constraints -> available transition sectors. Restricted typicality does not preserve the block algebra or establish the two-sided rate envelope.
repository_card.next_finite_task: Tabulate logical and nonlogical weights versus filling, then repeat a small-system rate scan over bath strength while directly checking the block-invariance residual. Distinguish static sum rules from fitted rates.
repository_card.falsifier: A nonzero invariance residual blocks the stated exponent transfer. Nonmonotonic bath dependence or loss of uniform spectral isolation invalidates an extrapolated maintenance floor.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: Non-Abelian string melting and thermalization in an open lattice gauge theory
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: model, thermalization discussion and strong-dephasing reduction
sources.source_claim: A tensor-network study couples 1+1D SU(2) gauge theory with matter to a gauge-preserving Lindblad bath. It finds nonmonotonic relaxation and derives an exclusion-process description in a strong-dephasing limit.
sources.limits: This is an open-system finite/truncated lattice setting, not pure 4D Euclidean Yang-Mills. A Liouvillian relaxation rate is not automatically a Hamiltonian gap, and the strong-dephasing expansion has its own regime.
